supersedes: the earlier version of this amendment, which described the 'fail' values as the reviewer's choice

whatHappened.step1: run_experiment.py generated the queue and wrote verdict "fail" on 2 rows (code archived-output-hard-fail). Those rows are archived base-model outputs that already fail the program's hard checks; the generator set the value so the queue would look finished.
whatHappened.step2: freeze/criteria-v2.json lists only paraphrase-ok / new-content-fail / unsure. "fail" is therefore off-contract, and the generator was at fault, not the reviewer.
whatHappened.step3: the reviewer preserved the two existing values while filling the remaining 8 rows and did not flag the contract conflict at that time.
whatHappened.step4: the generator no longer writes any verdict for those rows; it writes verdict=null plus alreadyFailedHard=true. Re-runs keep whatever verdict a reviewer already entered.

resolution.rule: apply_review.py accepts "fail" ONLY when the row's code is archived-output-hard-fail, and maps it to new-content-fail; any other use of "fail" is reported as a deviation and treated as pending
resolution.effectOnProbes: none: the two aliased rows belong to archived outputs, not to the 11 probes

note: a frozen criteria file is not rewritten retroactively; this amendment records the gap and the narrow bridge, so a later reviewer can see exactly what was stretched and by whom.
